exams: NEET UG for MBBS, BDS, BAMS and nursing (held at Kathmandu, fee Rs 9,500)
JEE Main for BTech and BArch at NITs and IIITs through DASA (Kathmandu centre, fee Rs 5,000 a paper, Session 1 on 22 to 30 January 2027)
CUET UG for central and state university BA, BSc and BCom seats (Kathmandu centre, fee Rs 4,500 for 3 subjects)
Private universities and deemed universities set their own tests or accept these scores

abroad_note_add.in: Entrance routes for a Nepali student (2026 cycle, see the exam entries for details): NEET UG for medicine, JEE Main then DASA for NIT and IIIT engineering (SAARC applicants pay USD 300 plus half the tuition, USD 2,300 first semester enrolment fee), CUET UG for central university arts, science and commerce. All three run a Kathmandu centre, so you sit the test at home; the foreign centre fee is much higher than the Indian fee (Rs 9,500 against Rs 1,700 for NEET). Medical and dental students also need the Nepal NOC and must pass the Nepal Medical Council licensing exam to practise in Nepal.

s-mgss.covers: NPR 24,000 per year (NPR 2,000 a month) for two years across Class 11 and 12, so NPR 48,000 at most, paid into a bank account the Embassy opens in your name. Applicants who get another scholarship are not eligible.
s-mgss.how: The 2026-27 window on goischolarship.com.np opened on 23 October 2026. The first Embassy notice closed it on 15 November 2026 (portal shut at 00.00 on 16 November), but the portal now says the last date was extended to 29 November 2026 at 23.59 hrs (checked on 19 November 2026), so you still have days left. You need a regular Class 11 place (not a diploma), at least 60 percent in SEE, and family income below NPR 200,000 a year; upload the SEE mark sheet and an income proof. Apply directly; the Embassy does not take applications through consultants or agents. Awardees send the Class 11 mark sheet and a promotion certificate by 31 December to continue in Class 12.

s-gjss.covers: NPR 48,000 a year for MBBS and BDS (5 years) and for BE, BTech, BArch and BAMS (4 years), and NPR 36,000 a year for 3 years for other bachelor courses, paid into a bank account the Embassy opens in your name. Continuation each year needs the mark sheet and a promotion certificate.
s-gjss.how: The 2026-27 window on goischolarship.com.np opened on 23 October 2026. The first Embassy notice closed it on 15 November 2026, but the portal banner now reads that the last date was extended to 29 November 2026 at 23.59 hrs (checked on 19 November 2026). You must be a regular first year bachelor student (not diploma) in a recognised Nepali institution, aged 17 to 22 on 1 July 2027, with a Class 12 mark sheet, family income below NPR 200,000 a year, and no other scholarship. Send the mark sheet and promotion certificate by 31 December each year to continue. Apply directly, not through agents.

guides_add.name: Study in India as a Nepali student: NEET, JEE Main or CUET
steps: Pick the course and the matching test: NEET UG for medicine, JEE Main for engineering and architecture, CUET UG for BA, BSc and BCom at central universities
Read the new NTA bulletin on neet.nta.nic.in, jeemain.nta.nic.in or cuet.nta.nic.in and register in the window, choosing Kathmandu as the exam city (JEE Main Session 1 closes on 22 November 2026)
Sit the test at the Kathmandu centre with your admit card and a valid ID
Apply for a seat: DASA on the DASA and CSAB portal for NIT and IIIT engineering, the Medical Counselling Committee or a private college for medicine, or the university itself for CUET courses
For medical study, get the NOC from the Ministry of Education before you pay the seat fee (noc.moest.gov.np)
Travel with your citizenship or passport; no student visa is needed under the 1950 Treaty

govt_add.name: NEET UG (India) for MBBS, BDS, BAMS and nursing seats in India
govt_add.level: The single national medical entrance test of India, run by the National Testing Agency (NTA). Nepali students take it at the Kathmandu centre
govt_add.need: +2 Science with Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Biotechnology and English; age 17 by 31 December of the admission year, no upper age limit
govt_add.age: 17 years or more by 31 December of the admission year
stages: Pen and paper test of 3 hours (180 minutes) on Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Zoology, +4 for a right answer and -1 for a wrong one, 720 marks, offered in 13 languages. The qualifying cut off is the 50th percentile for the general category.

Seat choice happens in the counselling of the Indian state or the Medical Counselling Committee, or directly in a private or deemed university. Foreign nationals mostly enter through the foreign national or management quota of a private or deemed college (hubintlglobal.com, studyinindiahub.com), so confirm the seat route per college.
subjects: Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Zoology from the NCERT Class 11 and 12 books
English plus the language of your choice for the paper
prep: Read the NCERT Biology books line by line; most Biology questions come straight from them
Fix a college list only from the National Medical Commission (NMC) recognised list, because the Nepal Medical Council licensing exam (NMCLE) needs a recognised degree
Get the Nepal no objection certificate for foreign study before you pay a seat fee (see the NOC guide)
govt_add.note: 2026 cycle: registration 8 February to 11 March 2026 (extended from 8 March), correction 12 to 14 March, fee Rs 9,500 (about NPR 15,200) for centres outside India against Rs 1,700 for a general candidate at an Indian centre, one of 14 foreign cities, with Kathmandu as city code 9907. The test planned for 3 May 2026 was held again on 21 June 2026 (Indian Express, Aakash notice of 7 June). NTA data for 2026 counted 927 foreign national registrants (msmunify.com). Nepali citizens need no visa to study in India (1950 Treaty), but the Indian degree only counts in Nepal after the NMCLE. The 2027 bulletin and dates are not out yet, so watch neet.nta.nic.in from about February.

govt_add.name: JEE Main and DASA (BTech and BArch seats at NITs and IIITs for foreign nationals)
govt_add.level: JEE Main is the entrance test for NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutes; DASA (Direct Admission of Students Abroad) is the Government of India scheme that gives foreign nationals extra seats there
govt_add.need: +2 or equivalent with Physics, Mathematics and one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Computer Science or Biology; 75 percent (or 7.5 CGPA) in the best five subjects for DASA 2026
govt_add.age: Born on or after 1 October 2001 for DASA UG 2026 (check the new brochure each year)
govt_add.body: National Testing Agency for JEE Main (jeemain.nta.nic.in); DASA coordinated by IIEST Shibpur with NIC for the Ministry of Education (dasanit.org, csab.nic.in)
stages: JEE Main Paper 1 (BE/BTech) or Paper 2A (BArch) or 2B (BPlanning)
Computer based test. Paper 1 has 75 questions for 300 marks with minus one for a wrong answer. Taken at the Kathmandu centre (city code ZZ05); the paper outside India is in English only.

Online on the DASA and CSAB portal. The DASA enrolment fee for the SAARC category is USD 2,300 (USD 300 non refundable registration plus USD 2,000 first semester tuition) and USD 4,300 for non SAARC applicants.
Two rounds on the JEE Main common rank list, in up to 15 percent supernumerary seats per programme at 31 NITs, IIEST Shibpur, 18 IIITs and other centrally funded institutes (2026 brochure).
subjects: Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (Class 11 and 12 NCERT level)
For BArch: Mathematics, aptitude and drawing
prep: Sit Session 1 in January and keep Session 2 in April as a second chance; the better rank counts
Ignore old pages that say DASA uses the SAT: the 2026 brochure (version 1.5) allots seats on the JEE Main rank only
DASA is not the same as JoSAA: JoSAA is the Indian citizen counselling, DASA is the separate foreign national pool
govt_add.note: JEE Main 2027: Session 1 on 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027 with 31 January as a buffer day; registration closes on 22 November 2026 at 11:50 pm IST (one site lists a late window to 26 November with Rs 500 extra, so read the NTA notice); Session 2 in April 2027 (applications expected 5 January to 3 February 2027, to be confirmed). Fee at a centre outside India: Rs 5,000 for a general male and Rs 4,000 for a general female per paper per session (about NPR 8,000 and 6,400); Rs 2,500 for SC, ST and PwD. DASA UG 2026 registration closed on 3 August 2026. SAARC applicants get half the tuition waived when the qualifying exam was passed in a SAARC country, which covers the NEB +2 (bodmaseducation.com). The seat tuition then follows the institute: about Rs 125,000 a year is the domestic level used for the Gulf quota (brilliantqatar.com).

govt_add.name: CUET UG (India central and state universities, BA, BSc, BCom and integrated courses)
govt_add.level: The Common University Entrance Test (Undergraduate) of the National Testing Agency, used by 280 plus universities in India; held at a Kathmandu centre
govt_add.need: Class 12 or equivalent (the NTA list accepts Cambridge A Level, IB and other boards; the NEB +2 is normally taken as equivalent but each university decides)
govt_add.age: No upper age limit at the NTA level; some university courses set one
stages: Up to 5 subjects chosen from 13 languages, 23 domain subjects and the General Test; +5 for a right answer and -1 for a wrong one. Offered in 13 mediums.

Each participating university publishes its own CUET subject combination and cut off. Foreign national seats are limited and run by the university or ICCR, so write to the international office before you pay.
subjects: Domain subjects such as Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, Economics, Accountancy, Business Studies, Political Science and History
prep: Pick the subjects your target university lists for your course; a wrong subject mix makes the score useless there
Read NCERT Class 12 books, since the domain papers follow that syllabus
Ask the university international office whether it admits foreign nationals on CUET or on another route
govt_add.note: 2026 cycle: notification 3 January 2026, registration to 30 January then extended to 4 February and reopened 23 to 26 February; the exam ran in mid May to early June (sources print 11 to 31 May and 13 May to 3 June). Fee: Rs 1,000 for a general candidate for up to 3 subjects in India, but Rs 4,500 for up to 3 subjects at a centre outside India plus Rs 1,800 for each extra subject (about NPR 7,200 and 2,900). Kathmandu is one of the foreign centres (ZZ05). The foreign centre list in 2026 had 14 to 15 cities. Treat the score as one of several routes: the ICCR and Embassy scholarships (see the ICCR entry) and private university direct admission stay open without it.

govt_add.name: Provincial Public Service Commissions (Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali, Sudurpashchim) and local government service
govt_add.level: Level 7 and 8 officer posts, plus lower levels, for provincial and local government service, set by the commission of each of the 7 provinces
govt_add.need: Bachelor for Level 7 (the post lists the exact degree, such as civil engineering, BSc Agriculture, BVSc, law or any bachelor for Section Officer); MBBS plus council registration for Level 8 Medical Officer
govt_add.age: 21 to 35 years, up to 40 for women and persons with disabilities, and 21 to 45 for health service posts (Koshi notice 106/2083-84)
govt_add.body: Provincial Public Service Commission of each province, for example psc.koshi.gov.np in Biratnagar
stages: Two papers for most technical posts (Medical Officer, Engineer, Veterinary, Livestock, Public Health, Lab) and three for Education Officer; four papers for Section Officer and Accounts Officer. Centre announced by the commission.
Computer skill, group assessment and interview
Held where the syllabus says so, after the written result. Open and inclusive candidates sit the first paper together.
subjects: General knowledge, province and local government law
Computer skills test for non technical posts
prep: Get the syllabus from the commission of your province, not from a federal PSC page
You can apply to more than one inclusive group, and you pay NPR 400 for each extra group in the Koshi notice
Qualification, age and council registration must be complete on the regular deadline; the double fee date does not extend them
govt_add.note: Koshi 2083/84 (notices 104, 105 and 106 published 2083/06/26): 69 competitive seats (49 technical and 20 non technical, 6 of them Level 8 Medical Officer) and 29 promotion posts for serving staff. Fee NPR 1,200 for Level 7 or 8 plus NPR 400 per extra group, regular deadline 2083/07/15, double fee deadline 2083/07/22, payment by 2083/07/23, online at the Koshi portal with PDF documents and both sides of the citizenship in JPG. Post wise written papers ran 2083/09/04 to 2083/10/25. Promotion forms (NPR 1,200 for Level 7, 2,000 for Level 9) are paper forms at the Biratnagar office and are not open competition. The other six provinces run their own calls, so fees and dates differ; the notice does not print a salary. An older blog prints NPR 300 and 400 for assistant level forms, so read each vacancy notice for the fee.

govt_note_add.e-mecee: Indian students apply to Nepal in the reverse way: for 2026/27 the MEC opened foreign applications on 10 August 2026, with the MECEE-BL track closing on 31 August (late until 7 September) and a NEET based sub category closing on 2 October 2026 with a fee of INR 5,000 (alladmission.co.in, bodmaseducation.com). A Nepali student who wants a seat in India sits NEET UG instead and still needs the Nepal NOC.

faq_add.q: Can a Nepali student sit NEET for MBBS in India, and where is the test held?
faq_add.a: Yes. NEET UG is the national medical entrance of India and it has a centre in Kathmandu (city code 9907), one of 14 foreign cities in 2026. Foreign nationals pay Rs 9,500 (about NPR 15,200) against Rs 1,700 for a general candidate at an Indian centre. You need +2 Science with Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English, age 17 by 31 December, and the 50th percentile to qualify. The 2026 test planned for 3 May was held again on 21 June 2026, so watch neet.nta.nic.in for the 2027 dates (about February). Get the Nepal NOC and remember that you must pass the Nepal Medical Council licensing exam to practise in Nepal.

faq_add.q: How do I get a BTech seat at an NIT or IIIT in India as a Nepali student?
faq_add.a: Take JEE Main (it has a Kathmandu centre, city code ZZ05), then apply through DASA (Direct Admission of Students Abroad), which gives foreign nationals up to 15 percent extra seats at 31 NITs, IIEST Shibpur, 18 IIITs and other centrally funded institutes. DASA UG 2026 needed 75 percent (or 7.5 CGPA) in the best five subjects with Physics, Mathematics and one more science subject, and birth on or after 1 October 2001. The 2026 brochure (version 1.5) allots seats on the JEE Main rank only, so ignore pages that still say SAT. The enrolment fee for the SAARC category was USD 2,300 (USD 300 registration plus USD 2,000 first semester tuition) against USD 4,300 for non SAARC applicants.

faq_add.q: When is JEE Main 2027 and how much does it cost from Nepal?
faq_add.a: Session 1 is on 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027 (31 January is a buffer day) and registration closes on 22 November 2026 at 11:50 pm IST, so it is closing this week. Session 2 is in April 2027, with applications expected 5 January to 3 February 2027 (to be confirmed by NTA). At a centre outside India, which includes Kathmandu, one paper costs Rs 5,000 for a general male and Rs 4,000 for a general female per session (about NPR 8,000 and 6,400). Both papers together cost Rs 10,000 and Rs 8,000. Paper 1 has 75 questions for 300 marks, computer based and in English only abroad.

faq_add.q: What is CUET UG and do Nepali students need it?
faq_add.a: CUET UG is the Common University Entrance Test of the National Testing Agency, used by more than 280 Indian universities for BA, BSc, BCom and integrated courses. Foreign nationals may sit it, and Kathmandu is one of the foreign centres (ZZ05). The fee outside India is Rs 4,500 for up to 3 subjects plus Rs 1,800 for each extra subject (about NPR 7,200 plus NPR 2,900), against Rs 1,000 for a general candidate in India. The 2026 cycle took registrations from 3 January to late February. You only need it if your target university asks for it for foreign national seats, so email its international office before you pay.

faq_add.q: Do I need a visa or a work permit to study in India as a Nepali citizen?
faq_add.a: No. Under the 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, Nepali and Indian nationals have the same privileges in residence and movement, so you travel with your citizenship certificate or passport and need no student visa or work permit. Government posts such as IAS and property purchases are the exceptions. The real hurdles are the entrance test (NEET, JEE Main or CUET), the seat fee, and for medicine and dentistry the Nepal NOC and the later Nepal Medical Council licensing exam.

faq_add.q: Is the MGSS and GJSS scholarship deadline still open?
faq_add.a: Yes, for a few more days. The first Embassy of India notice closed applications on 15 November 2026, but the official portal goischolarship.com.np now says the last date was extended to 29 November 2026 at 23:59. MGSS gives NPR 24,000 a year for 2 years to Class 11 students with at least 60 percent in SEE and family income below NPR 200,000. GJSS gives NPR 48,000 a year (MBBS, BDS, BE, BTech, BArch, BAMS) or NPR 36,000 a year (other bachelor courses) to first year bachelor students aged 17 to 22 on 1 July 2027. Apply yourself; the Embassy does not use agents.

faq_add.q: What is a provincial Lok Sewa Aayog and how is it different from the federal one?
faq_add.a: Each of the 7 provinces has its own Provincial Public Service Commission that hires for provincial and local government service, separate from the federal Public Service Commission. Koshi advertised 69 competitive seats on 2083/06/26: 49 technical (6 Level 8 Medical Officers and 43 Level 7 engineers, agriculture, veterinary, education, public health and lab posts) and 20 non technical (Section Officer, Accounts Officer and Law Officer). The fee was NPR 1,200 plus NPR 400 per extra group; ages 21 to 35, up to 40 for women and persons with disabilities and 45 for health posts. Dates and fees differ between provinces, so use the syllabus and notice of your own commission.

faq_add.q: Which degrees can apply for Koshi provincial Level 7 posts?
faq_add.a: It depends on the post (Koshi notice 106/2083-84): civil engineering for Engineer; BSc Agriculture for Agriculture Extension, Horticulture and Crop Development Officer; BVSc and AH or DVM for Veterinary Officer; BSc Animal Science, Dairy Science or BVSc for Livestock Development Officer; a bachelor in Education for Education Officer; a bachelor in Public Health or Medical Laboratory Technology with council registration for those posts; any bachelor for Section Officer; management, commerce or business administration (or economics, mathematics or statistics major) for Accounts Officer; and law for Law Officer. MBBS with council registration is needed for Level 8 Medical Officer.

faq_add.q: Why is the foreign exam centre fee for Indian tests so high?
faq_add.a: NTA sets a higher fee for centres outside India: NEET UG Rs 9,500 against Rs 1,700, JEE Main Rs 5,000 a paper against Rs 1,000 for a general male candidate in India, and CUET UG Rs 4,500 for 3 subjects against Rs 1,000. At the fixed rate of NPR 1.6 per INR that is about NPR 15,200, NPR 8,000 and NPR 7,200. The Kathmandu centre is used by all three, so you save the travel, but budget the fee before you register.

faq_add.q: Can an Indian student study MBBS in Nepal through NEET?
faq_add.a: Yes, in the other direction. For 2026/27 the Medical Education Commission of Nepal took foreign applications from 10 August 2026 with two sub categories: sub category I through the MECEE-BL entrance (closing on 31 August, late fee until 7 September) and sub category II through a NEET score at the 50th percentile or above (closing on 2 October 2026, fee INR 5,000). Nepali students use the MECEE-BL, not NEET, for Nepali seats; a Nepali who wants an Indian seat sits NEET UG itself.
